chunks: He said: And Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran narrated to me from Yahya ibn al-Qasim al-Hazza and others, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Dawud ibn Zarbi, who said:

The Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) sent for me while he was in prison and said: Go to that man, meaning Yahya ibn Khalid, and say to him: So-and-so says: What drove you to what you did? You exiled me from my country and separated me from my family. I went to him and informed him. He said: Zubayda is divorced! He swore with the strongest oaths and said: I wish he had paid two million [dirhams] right now and you had been released. I returned to him and conveyed the message. He said: Go back to him and say to him: He says to you: By God, you will definitely release me or I will leave on my own accord.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The Abd al-Salih (a title for Imam Musa al-Kadim)

ai.seo_question: What was the interaction between Imam Musa al-Kadim and Yahya ibn Khalid during his imprisonment?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the political tension between the Abbasid vizier Yahya ibn Khalid and Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), illustrating the Imam's dignified endurance of exile. The exchange underscores the theme of divine justice amidst worldly power, as the Imam’s calm defiance contrasts with the vizier’s attempt to secure his release through ransom, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of the Imam as the focal point of spiritual authority even in confinement.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 39 - Narrated to me Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Humran from Yahya bin Qasim Hazza etc. from Jamil bin Salih from Dawood bin Zarbi that he said:

When Abde Salih, Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s) was in prison, he summoned me and said: Go to that man, Yahya bin Khalid Barmaki and say: So and so says: ‘What is the reason that you should do this; you have made me homeless and separated me from my family and children?’ I went to Yahya and informed him of this. Yahya exclaimed: Zubaida [wife of Harun] is being divorced! He swore many times and said: ‘I wish to pay two million dirhams as ransom and free you!’ I returned to the Imam and mentioned the matter; he said: Go and tell him: So and so says: By God, you will definitely release me or I would leave of my own accord.
